Scan targets for XSS

Usage: dalfox scan [OPTIONS] [TARGET]...

Options:
      --config <FILE>
          Path to a config file (TOML or JSON). Overrides default search path

      --debug
          Enable debug logging (show DBG lines)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

INPUT:
  -i, --input-type <INPUT_TYPE>
          Input type: auto, url, file, pipe, raw-http, har
          
          [default: auto]

      --dedup-urls <MODE>
          Target deduplication [default: exact]: exact (drop byte-identical URL+method), signature (also collapse URLs that differ only in parameter values — keys on method+host+path+parameter names), off (scan every input line)
          
          [possible values: exact, signature, off]

      --state-file <PATH>
          Record which targets finished to PATH and skip them when the same scan is re-run, so an interrupted mass scan resumes instead of restarting. Only fully completed targets are skipped; ones cut short by Ctrl-C or --scan-timeout are retried. Example: --state-file scan.state

OUTPUT:
  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: json, jsonl, plain, markdown, sarif, toml
          
          [default: plain]
          [possible values: plain, json, jsonl, markdown, sarif, toml]

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Write output to a file. Example: -o 'output.txt'

      --include-request
          Include HTTP request information in output

      --include-response
          Include HTTP response information in output

      --include-all
          Include both HTTP request and response information in output (equivalent to --include-request --include-response)

      --no-color
          Disable colored output (also respects NO_COLOR env var)

  -S, --silence
          Silence all logs except POC output to STDOUT

      --dry-run
          Dry-run mode: parse targets, run parameter discovery, and report what would be scanned without sending attack payloads. Outputs target count, discovered parameters, and estimated request count

      --stream-findings
          Emit each finding (POC + Issue / Payload / Line) the moment it is verified, instead of waiting for end-of-scan. Useful for long scans where you want immediate feedback; off by default so the default flow shows findings after `WRN XSS found N XSS`

      --poc-type <POC_TYPE>
          POC output type: plain, curl, httpie, http-request
          
          [default: plain]
          [possible values: plain, curl, httpie, http-request]

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Limit the number of results to display (must be >=1). Example: --limit 10

      --limit-result-type <LIMIT_RESULT_TYPE>
          Filter which finding types count toward --limit: all (default), v (vulnerable), r (reflected), a (AST DOM XSS), i (informational). Example: --limit-result-type v
          
          [default: all]
          [possible values: all, v, r, a, i, V, R, A, I]

      --only-poc <ONLY_POC>
          Filter output to show only specific finding types (comma-separated). Options: v (vulnerable), r (reflected), a (AST DOM XSS), i (informational). Example: --only-poc "v,r"
          
          [possible values: v, r, a, i, V, R, A, I]

      --baseline <BASELINE>
          Diff against a previous dalfox JSON/JSONL report and report only findings new since it. The baseline is an ordinary `--format json --output` report. Example: --baseline baseline.json

      --baseline-mode <MODE>
          What --baseline does with already-known findings [default: filter]: filter (drop them, so the exit code gates on new findings only) or annotate (keep them and mark each `new`). Example: --baseline-mode annotate
          
          [possible values: filter, annotate]

TARGETS:
  -p, --param <PARAM>
          Specify parameter names to analyze (e.g., -p sort -p id:query). Types: query, body, json, cookie, header

  -d, --data <DATA>
          HTTP request body data

  -H, --headers <HEADERS>
          HTTP headers (can be specified multiple times)

      --cookies <COOKIES>
          Cookies (can be specified multiple times)

  -X, --method <METHOD>
          Override the HTTP method. Example: -X 'PUT' (default "GET")
          
          [default: GET]

      --user-agent <USER_AGENT>
          Set a custom User-Agent header. Example: --user-agent 'Mozilla/5.0'

      --cookie-from-raw <COOKIE_FROM_RAW>
          Load cookies from a raw HTTP request file. Example: --cookie-from-raw 'request.txt'

  [TARGET]...
          Targets (URLs or file paths)

SESSION:
      --session-check <REGEX>
          Regex that must keep matching the response body for the session to be considered alive (e.g. --session-check 'Sign out'). Authoritative: when set, the built-in heuristics (401/403, login redirect, appearing login form) are not consulted. Without it, session monitoring still runs automatically whenever credentials are supplied via --cookies, --cookie-from-raw, or a Cookie/Authorization header

      --session-check-url <URL>
          Probe this URL instead of the scan target when re-validating the session. Useful when the target itself is public but the app exposes a cheap authenticated endpoint. Example: --session-check-url 'https://app/me'

      --on-session-loss <POLICY>
          What to do when the session is detected as lost [default: abort]: abort stops the affected target and skips the rest of that host; continue keeps scanning. Either way the target is reported as `incomplete` / SESSION_LOST instead of a misleading "clean"
          
          [possible values: abort, continue]

SCOPE:
      --include-url <INCLUDE_URL>
          Include only URLs matching these patterns (regex, can be specified multiple times)

      --exclude-url <EXCLUDE_URL>
          Exclude URLs matching these patterns (regex, can be specified multiple times)

      --ignore-param <IGNORE_PARAM>

          Only perform parameter discovery (skip XSS scanning)

      --skip-discovery
          Skip all discovery checks

      --skip-reflection-header

      --skip-reflection-path

PARAMETER MINING:

      --skip-mining
          Skip all mining

      --skip-mining-dict
          Skip dictionary-based mining

      --skip-mining-dom
          Skip mining parameter names from HTML input id/name attributes. Does NOT disable DOM-XSS static analysis of inline scripts (the `[A]` findings) — use --skip-ast-analysis for that

NETWORK:
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>
          Per-request timeout in seconds (network only; does not bound total scan time)
          
          [default: 10]

      --scan-timeout <SCAN_TIMEOUT>
          Hard wall-clock cap per target for the payload-injection (scan) stage in seconds. When set, dalfox stops a target's payload-injection stage once this budget is exceeded — useful when many sequential phases each pay the per-request `--timeout` cost against a partially-hung endpoint. Scope note: this caps ONLY the injection stage. The earlier preflight and parameter-analysis (discovery + mining) phases are bounded separately by `--timeout` × request-count, NOT by this wall-clock cap, so a slow target can overshoot this budget during analysis. 0 disables (default)
          
          [default: 0]

      --delay <DELAY>
          Delay in milliseconds
          
          [default: 0]

  -r, --rate-limit <RATE_LIMIT>
          Cap the global outbound request rate in requests/second, shared across all workers and targets (0 = unlimited). Unlike --delay (which only spaces a single worker's requests), this bounds the total in-flight burst from workers × concurrent targets — friendlier to shared-IP / edge WAF thresholds. Example: --rate-limit 20
          
          [default: 0]
          [alias: --rl]

      --retries <RETRIES>
          Retry failed requests on HTTP 5xx and transient transport errors (timeouts, connection resets) up to this many times (0 = off). HTTP 429 is always retried regardless of this value. Example: --retries 2
          
          [default: 0]

      --retry-delay <RETRY_DELAY>
          Base delay (ms) for the exponential backoff between retries (--retries). Doubles each attempt and is capped internally; a server Retry-After header takes precedence on 429. Example: --retry-delay 500
          
          [default: 1000]

      --proxy <PROXY>
          Proxy URL (e.g., http://localhost:8080, socks5://localhost:9050)

      --insecure[=<INSECURE>]
          Skip TLS/SSL certificate verification, accepting self-signed, expired, or hostname-mismatched certs. Enabled by default for scanner use; pass `--insecure=false` to enforce certificate validation. Example: --insecure=false
          
          Stored as Option so presence is distinguishable from the default: `None` means the user didn't pass the flag (config may set it; the effective value is `unwrap_or(true)`), while `Some(_)` is an explicit CLI choice that always wins over config — in either direction.
          
          [possible values: true, false]

  -F, --follow-redirects
          Follow HTTP redirects. Example: -F

      --ignore-return <IGNORE_RETURN>
          Ignore specific HTTP status codes during scanning (comma-separated). Example: --ignore-return 302,403,404

ENGINE:
      --workers <WORKERS>
          Number of concurrent workers
          
          [default: 50]

      --max-concurrent-targets <MAX_CONCURRENT_TARGETS>
          Maximum number of concurrent targets to scan
          
          [default: 50]

      --max-targets-per-host <MAX_TARGETS_PER_HOST>
          Maximum number of targets per host
          
          [default: 100]

XSS SCANNING:
  -e, --encoders <ENCODERS>
          Specify payload encoders to use (comma-separated). Options: none, url, 2url, 3url, 4url, html, htmlpad, base64, unicode, zwsp. Default: url,html
          
          [default: url html]
          [possible values: none, url, 2url, 3url, 4url, html, htmlpad, base64, unicode, zwsp]

      --remote-payloads <REMOTE_PAYLOADS>
          Fetch remote XSS payloads from providers (comma-separated). Options: portswigger, payloadbox

      --custom-blind-xss-payload <CUSTOM_BLIND_XSS_PAYLOAD>
          Load custom blind XSS payloads from a file. Example: --custom-blind-xss-payload 'payloads.txt'

  -b, --blind <BLIND_CALLBACK_URL>
          Blind XSS callback URL. Example: -b 'https://example.com/callback'

      --blind-oob[=<BLIND_OOB>...]

      --blind-oob-secret <BLIND_OOB_SECRET>
          Auth token (secret) for a self-hosted interactsh server; sent as the Authorization header on register/poll/deregister

          Only test custom payloads. Example: --only-custom-payload --custom-payload=p.txt

      --custom-alert-value <CUSTOM_ALERT_VALUE>

      --custom-alert-type <CUSTOM_ALERT_TYPE>
          Custom alert function type. Options: none (keep original), str (wrap value in quotes). Default: "none"
          
          [default: none]
          [possible values: none, str]

      --inject-marker <INJECT_MARKER>
          Custom injection point marker. Replace this string with payloads in URL/headers/body. Example: --inject-marker 'FUZZ' with URL 'http://example.com/?q=FUZZ'

Note: the cap applies to the base catalog; WAF-bypass mutation/encoder expansion and a small set of shared CSP-bypass / tech-specific payloads are added afterwards (and never trimmed), so the actual per-parameter total can exceed this value — substantially so when a WAF bypass strategy is active. Usage: dalfox payload [OPTIONS] [SELECTOR]

            - dom-clobbering: print DOM clobbering payloads
            - mxss: print mutation-XSS / sanitizer-bypass payloads
            - blind: print blind-XSS skeletons ({} = your OOB callback URL)

scan.--config: Path to a config file (TOML or JSON). Overrides default search path
scan.--input-type: Input type: auto, url, file, pipe, raw-http, har
scan.--dedup-urls: Target deduplication [default: exact]: exact (drop byte-identical URL+method), signature (also collapse URLs that differ only in parameter values — keys on method+host+path+parameter names), off (scan every input line)
scan.--state-file: Record which targets finished to PATH and skip them when the same scan is re-run, so an interrupted mass scan resumes instead of restarting. Only fully completed targets are skipped; ones cut short by Ctrl-C or --scan-timeout are retried. Example: --state-file scan.state
scan.--format: Output format: json, jsonl, plain, markdown, sarif, toml
scan.--output: Write output to a file. Example: -o 'output.txt'
scan.--include-request: Include HTTP request information in output
scan.--include-response: Include HTTP response information in output
scan.--include-all: Include both HTTP request and response information in output (equivalent to --include-request --include-response)
scan.--no-color: Disable colored output (also respects NO_COLOR env var)
scan.--silence: Silence all logs except POC output to STDOUT
scan.--dry-run: Dry-run mode: parse targets, run parameter discovery, and report what would be scanned without sending attack payloads. Outputs target count, discovered parameters, and estimated request count
scan.--stream-findings: Emit each finding (POC + Issue / Payload / Line) the moment it is verified, instead of waiting for end-of-scan. Useful for long scans where you want immediate feedback; off by default so the default flow shows findings after `WRN XSS found N XSS`
scan.--poc-type: POC output type: plain, curl, httpie, http-request
scan.--limit: Limit the number of results to display (must be >=1). Example: --limit 10
scan.--limit-result-type: Filter which finding types count toward --limit: all (default), v (vulnerable), r (reflected), a (AST DOM XSS), i (informational). Example: --limit-result-type v
scan.--only-poc: Filter output to show only specific finding types (comma-separated). Options: v (vulnerable), r (reflected), a (AST DOM XSS), i (informational). Example: --only-poc "v,r"
scan.--baseline: Diff against a previous dalfox JSON/JSONL report and report only findings new since it. The baseline is an ordinary `--format json --output` report. Example: --baseline baseline.json
scan.--baseline-mode: What --baseline does with already-known findings [default: filter]: filter (drop them, so the exit code gates on new findings only) or annotate (keep them and mark each `new`). Example: --baseline-mode annotate
scan.--param: Specify parameter names to analyze (e.g., -p sort -p id:query). Types: query, body, json, cookie, header
scan.--headers: HTTP headers (can be specified multiple times)
scan.--user-agent: Set a custom User-Agent header. Example: --user-agent 'Mozilla/5.0'
scan.--cookie-from-raw: Load cookies from a raw HTTP request file. Example: --cookie-from-raw 'request.txt'
scan.--session-check: Regex that must keep matching the response body for the session to be considered alive (e.g. --session-check 'Sign out'). Authoritative: when set, the built-in heuristics (401/403, login redirect, appearing login form) are not consulted. Without it, session monitoring still runs automatically whenever credentials are supplied via --cookies, --cookie-from-raw, or a Cookie/Authorization header
scan.--session-check-url: Probe this URL instead of the scan target when re-validating the session. Useful when the target itself is public but the app exposes a cheap authenticated endpoint. Example: --session-check-url 'https://app/me'
scan.--on-session-loss: What to do when the session is detected as lost [default: abort]: abort stops the affected target and skips the rest of that host; continue keeps scanning. Either way the target is reported as `incomplete` / SESSION_LOST instead of a misleading "clean"
scan.--include-url: Include only URLs matching these patterns (regex, can be specified multiple times)
scan.--exclude-url: Exclude URLs matching these patterns (regex, can be specified multiple times)
scan.--ignore-param: Ignore specific parameters during scanning (can be specified multiple times)
scan.--out-of-scope: Exclude targets whose domain matches these patterns (supports wildcards, e.g. *.dev.example.com)
scan.--out-of-scope-file: Load out-of-scope domains from a file (one per line, supports wildcards)
scan.--only-discovery: Only perform parameter discovery (skip XSS scanning)
scan.--mining-dict-word: Dictionary analysis with wordlist file path
scan.--remote-wordlists: Fetch remote parameter wordlists from providers (comma-separated). Options: burp, assetnote
scan.--skip-mining-dom: Skip mining parameter names from HTML input id/name attributes. Does NOT disable DOM-XSS static analysis of inline scripts (the `[A]` findings) — use --skip-ast-analysis for that
scan.--timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds (network only; does not bound total scan time)
scan.--scan-timeout: Hard wall-clock cap per target for the payload-injection (scan) stage in seconds. When set, dalfox stops a target's payload-injection stage once this budget is exceeded — useful when many sequential phases each pay the per-request `--timeout` cost against a partially-hung endpoint. Scope note: this caps ONLY the injection stage. The earlier preflight and parameter-analysis (discovery + mining) phases are bounded separately by `--timeout` × request-count, NOT by this wall-clock cap, so a slow target can overshoot this budget during analysis. 0 disables (default)
scan.--rate-limit: Cap the global outbound request rate in requests/second, shared across all workers and targets (0 = unlimited). Unlike --delay (which only spaces a single worker's requests), this bounds the total in-flight burst from workers × concurrent targets — friendlier to shared-IP / edge WAF thresholds. Example: --rate-limit 20
scan.--retries: Retry failed requests on HTTP 5xx and transient transport errors (timeouts, connection resets) up to this many times (0 = off). HTTP 429 is always retried regardless of this value. Example: --retries 2
scan.--retry-delay: Base delay (ms) for the exponential backoff between retries (--retries). Doubles each attempt and is capped internally; a server Retry-After header takes precedence on 429. Example: --retry-delay 500
scan.--insecure: Skip TLS/SSL certificate verification, accepting self-signed, expired, or hostname-mismatched certs. Enabled by default for scanner use; pass `--insecure=false` to enforce certificate validation. Example: --insecure=false
scan.--ignore-return: Ignore specific HTTP status codes during scanning (comma-separated). Example: --ignore-return 302,403,404
scan.--max-concurrent-targets: Maximum number of concurrent targets to scan
scan.--max-targets-per-host: Maximum number of targets per host
scan.--encoders: Specify payload encoders to use (comma-separated). Options: none, url, 2url, 3url, 4url, html, htmlpad, base64, unicode, zwsp. Default: url,html
scan.--remote-payloads: Fetch remote XSS payloads from providers (comma-separated). Options: portswigger, payloadbox
scan.--custom-blind-xss-payload: Load custom blind XSS payloads from a file. Example: --custom-blind-xss-payload 'payloads.txt'
scan.--blind-oob: Enable OOB blind XSS via interactsh. Optional comma-separated server domains (default: public servers). Example: --blind-oob=oast.fun,oast.me
scan.--blind-oob-secret: Auth token (secret) for a self-hosted interactsh server; sent as the Authorization header on register/poll/deregister
scan.--blind-oob-wait: Seconds to keep polling for OOB callbacks after all payloads are sent (default 30; 0 = no extra end-of-scan wait)
scan.--custom-payload: Load custom payloads from a file. Example: --custom-payload 'payloads.txt'
scan.--custom-alert-value: Custom value for alert/prompt/confirm in payloads. Default: "1". Example: --custom-alert-value 'document.domain'
scan.--custom-alert-type: Custom alert function type. Options: none (keep original), str (wrap value in quotes). Default: "none"
scan.--inject-marker: Custom injection point marker. Replace this string with payloads in URL/headers/body. Example: --inject-marker 'FUZZ' with URL 'http://example.com/?q=FUZZ'
scan.--max-payloads-per-param: Cap the number of base payloads tested per parameter (reflection set and DOM-verification set are each capped independently). 0 (default) applies a built-in safety cap of 3000 per set unless --deep-scan is set; pass an explicit value to override, or --deep-scan for a truly unlimited run. Bounds the request fan-out on large attack surfaces and on endpoints that reflect every payload (self-/canonical-link echoes) without verifying. Note: the cap applies to the base catalog; WAF-bypass mutation/encoder expansion and a small set of shared CSP-bypass / tech-specific payloads are added afterwards (and never trimmed), so the actual per-parameter total can exceed this value — substantially so when a WAF bypass strategy is active. Use --deep-scan only to lift the built-in default cap
scan.--deep-scan: Perform deep scanning - test all payloads even after finding XSS
scan.--sxss-url: URL to check for Stored XSS reflection. When omitted with --sxss, auto-detects from form discovery context
scan.--sxss-method: HTTP method for checking Stored XSS (default "GET")
scan.--sxss-retries: Number of times to re-check the Stored XSS URL to handle slow session/content propagation. Each retry waits 500ms * attempt_index
scan.--skip-ast-analysis: Skip AST-based DOM XSS detection — the source→sink analysis of JavaScript in responses that emits [A] findings. This is the flag that silences them; --skip-mining-dom does not
scan.--analyze-external-js: Fetch and AST-analyze same-origin external <script src> bundles for DOM-XSS (off by default to preserve request budget)
scan.--hpp: Enable HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP) — duplicate query params to bypass WAF
scan.--detect-outdated-libs: Also report outdated / known-vulnerable JS libraries (informational, CWE-1104). Off by default: dalfox focuses on verified XSS; this is an opt-in retire.js-style add-on that inspects <script> tags (0 extra requests)
scan.--waf-bypass: WAF bypass mode: auto (detect+bypass), force (use --force-waf), off (detect-only; no payload mutations). Default: auto
scan.--skip-waf-probe: Skip WAF fingerprinting probes (header-only detection, no provocation request)
scan.--force-waf: Force a specific WAF type for bypass strategies (e.g., cloudflare, akamai, modsecurity)
scan.--waf-evasion: Adaptive WAF evasion: when a WAF is detected, randomize inter-request timing (jitter) and escalate a cooldown pause on clusters of blocked responses, instead of the old blunt workers=1/delay=3000 preset. Pairs well with --rate-limit. The per-WAF pacing hint is applied automatically on detection even without this flag
scan.--waf-min-confidence: Discard WAF fingerprints below this confidence (0.0–1.0). Default (0.3) filters weak signals like `Server: Google Frontend` (0.15 — emitted by every Google-hosted property regardless of Cloud Armor) and generic "Request blocked" body markers. Real WAF signatures (Cloudflare 0.9+, AWS WAF 0.95) are kept. Pass `--waf-min-confidence 0.0` to keep every match

server.--scan-timeout: Server-wide cap on each scan's total wall-clock runtime, in seconds (0 or unset = unbounded). server.--max-body-bytes: Maximum accepted request-body size (bytes) for POST /scan and /preflight. Replaces axum's implicit 2 MiB default with an explicit, documented bound
server.--allowed-origins: Comma-separated list of allowed origins for CORS. Supports: - "*" wildcard (match all) - exact origins (http://localhost:3000) - "regex:<pattern>" for regex

Powerful open-source XSS scanner

Usage: dalfox [COMMAND] [TARGET] <FLAGS>
e.g., dalfox scan https://dalfox.hahwul.com

Commands:
  scan     Scan targets for XSS
  server   Run API/server mode
  payload  Manage or enumerate payloads
  mcp      Run MCP stdio server (Model Context Protocol) exposing Dalfox tools
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [TARGET]...  Targets (when no subcommand is provided, defaults to scan)

Options:
      --config <FILE>  Path to a config file (TOML or JSON). Overrides default search path
      --debug          Enable debug logging (show DBG lines)
      --no-color       Disable colored output (also respects NO_COLOR env var)
  -S, --silence        Silence all logs except POC output to STDOUT
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version

--api-key.help: Specify the API key for server authentication. Example: --api-key 'your-secret-key'

--blind.help: Specify a blind XSS callback URL. Example: -b 'https://your-callback-url.com'

--config.help: Path to a config file (TOML or JSON). Overrides default search path

--context-aware.help: Enable context-aware payload selection for better XSS detection. Example: --context-aware

--cookie.help: Add custom cookies to the request. Example: -C 'sessionid=abc123'

--cookie-from-raw.help: lift cookies from a captured request file

--custom-alert-type.help: Set a custom alert type. Example: --custom-alert-type 'str,none'

--custom-alert-value.help: Set a custom alert value. Example: --custom-alert-value 'document.cookie'

--custom-blind-xss-payload.help: Load custom blind XSS payloads from a file. Example: --custom-blind-xss-payload 'payloads.txt'

--custom-payload.help: Load custom payloads from a file. Example: --custom-payload 'payloads.txt'

--data.help: Send body data with the request (supports all HTTP methods). Body can be form (key=value&...) or JSON. Example: -d 'username=admin&password=admin' or -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin"}'

--deep-domxss.help: Enable deep DOM XSS testing with more payloads (slow). Example: --deep-domxss

--delay.help: Set the delay between requests to the same host in milliseconds. Example: --delay 1000

--detailed-analysis.help: Enable detailed parameter analysis for better XSS detection. Example: --detailed-analysis

--entity-event-handler.help: Enumerate event handlers for XSS. Example: --entity-event-handler

--entity-gf.help: Enumerate parameters from GF-Patterns for XSS. Example: --entity-gf

--entity-special-chars.help: Enumerate special characters for XSS. Example: --entity-special-chars

--entity-useful-tags.help: Enumerate useful tags for XSS. Example: --entity-useful-tags

--fast-scan.help: Enable fast scanning mode for URL lists. Example: --fast-scan

--force-headless-verification.help: Force headless browser-based verification, useful when automatic detection fails or to override default behavior. Example: --force-headless-verification

--format.help: Set the output format. Supported: plain, json, jsonl. Example: --format 'json'

--found-action.help: Execute a command when a vulnerability is found. Example: --found-action './notify.sh'

--found-action-shell.help: Specify the shell to use for the found action. Example: --found-action-shell 'bash'

--grep.help: Use a custom grepping file. Example: --grep './samples/sample_grep.json'

--har-file-path.help: Specify the path to save HAR files of scan requests. Example: --har-file-path 'scan.har'

--header.help: Add custom headers to the request. Example: -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'

--host.help: Specify the address to bind the server to. Example: --host '0.0.0.0'

--http.help: Force HTTP on raw data mode. Example: --http

--ignore-param.help: Ignore specific parameters during scanning. Example: --ignore-param 'api_token' --ignore-param 'csrf_token'

--ignore-return.help: drop responses with these status codes before reflection analysis (comma-separated)

--include-request.help: / `--include-response` — embed raw HTTP in JSON output (large); `--include-all` is the shortcut for both

--limit.help: caps total findings; pair with `--limit-result-type v` to only count verified findings

--limit-result.help: Stop scanning after N findings (0 = unlimited). Example: --limit-result 1

--limit-result-type.help: Set finding type filter for --limit-result. Supported: all, v, r. Example: --limit-result-type 'v'

--magic-char-test.help: Enable magic character testing for manual XSS analysis. Example: --magic-char-test

--make-bulk.help: Generate bulk payloads for stored XSS. Example: --make-bulk

--mass.help: Enable parallel scanning in N*Host mode (only shows PoC code). Example: --mass

--mass-worker.help: Set the number of parallel workers for --mass and --multicast options. Example: --mass-worker 10

--max-cpu.help: Set the maximum number of CPUs to use. Example: --max-cpu 1

--mining-dict-word.help: Specify a custom wordlist file for parameter mining. Example: -W 'wordlist.txt'

--multicast.help: Enable parallel scanning in N*Host mode (only shows PoC code). Example: --multicast

--no-color.help: Disable colored output (also respects NO_COLOR env var)

--only-discovery.help: Only perform parameter analysis, skip XSS scanning. Example: --only-discovery

--only-poc.help: Show only the PoC code for the specified pattern. Supported: g (grep), r (reflected), v (verified). Example: --only-poc 'g,v'

--out-of-scope.help: Exclude domains from scanning. Supports wildcards. Example: --out-of-scope 'stg.example.com' --out-of-scope '*.dev.example.com'

--out-of-scope-file.help: Load out-of-scope domains from a file (one per line). Example: --out-of-scope-file 'exclusions.txt'

--output.help: Write output to a file. Example: -o 'output.txt'

--output-all.help: Enable all log write mode (output to file or stdout). Example: --output-all

--output-request.help: Include raw HTTP requests in the results. Example: --output-request

--output-response.help: Include raw HTTP responses in the results. Example: --output-response

--port.help: Specify the port to bind the server to. Example: --port 6664

--proxy.help: Send all requests through a proxy server. Example: --proxy 'http://127.0.0.1:8080'

--rate-limit.help: cap every scan's outbound request rate (protects targets).

--rawdata.help: [FORMAT] Use raw data from Burp/ZAP. Example: --rawdata

--remote-payloadbox.help: Enumerate payloads from Payloadbox's XSS payloads. Example: --remote-payloadbox

--remote-payloads.help: Use remote payloads for XSS testing. Supported: portswigger, payloadbox. Example: --remote-payloads 'portswigger,payloadbox'

--remote-portswigger.help: Enumerate payloads from PortSwigger's XSS cheatsheet. Example: --remote-portswigger

--remote-wordlists.help: Use remote wordlists for parameter mining. Supported: burp, assetnote. Example: --remote-wordlists 'burp'

--report-format.help: Set the format of the report. Supported: plain, json, markdown, md. Example: --report-format 'json'

--request-method.help: Specify the HTTP request method to send to the server. Example: --request-method 'POST'

--scan-timeout.help: hard wall-clock budget per scan; bounds long or

--sequence.help: Set the initial sequence number for the trigger URL. Example: --trigger 'https://example.com/view?no=SEQNC' --sequence 3

--silence.help: Silence all logs except POC output to STDOUT

--silence-force.help: Only print PoC code, suppress progress output. Example: --silence-force

--skip-bav.help: Skip Basic Another Vulnerability (BAV) analysis. Example: --skip-bav

--skip-discovery.help: Skip the entire discovery phase, proceeding directly to XSS scanning. Requires -p flag to specify parameters. Example: --skip-discovery -p 'username'

--skip-headless.help: Skip headless browser-based scanning (DOM XSS and inJS verification). Example: --skip-headless

--sxss-retries.help: how many times to poll the sxss-url (default 3); raise for slow-propagating apps

--trigger.help: Specify the URL to check after injecting SXSS code. Example: --trigger 'https://example.com/profile'

--type.help: Specify the server type. Example: --type 'rest' or --type 'mcp'

--use-bav.help: Enable Basic Another Vulnerability (BAV) analysis. Example: --use-bav

--user-agent.help: Set a custom User-Agent header. Example: --user-agent 'Mozilla/5.0'

--waf-bypass.help: `auto` probes first then bypasses, `force` applies bypass without probing (pair with `--force-waf cloudflare` etc. to pin a WAF), `off` disables the feature

--waf-evasion.help: Enable WAF evasion by adjusting speed when detecting WAF (worker=1, delay=3s). Example: --waf-evasion

--worker.help: Set the number of concurrent workers. Example: -w 100

--workers.help: (default) — lower for politeness, higher for speed; no short alias

dalfox.help: Dalfox is a powerful open-source XSS scanner and utility focused on automation.

file.help: Use file mode (targets list or raw HTTP request data)

payload.help: Payload mode, make and enum payloads

scan.--config: Path to a config file (TOML or JSON). Overrides default search path
scan.--input-type: Input type: auto, url, file, pipe, raw-http, har
scan.--dedup-urls: Target deduplication [default: exact]: exact (drop byte-identical URL+method), signature (also collapse URLs that differ only in parameter values — keys on method+host+path+parameter names), off (scan every input line)
scan.--state-file: Record which targets finished to PATH and skip them when the same scan is re-run, so an interrupted mass scan resumes instead of restarting. Only fully completed targets are skipped; ones cut short by Ctrl-C or --scan-timeout are retried. Example: --state-file scan.state
scan.--format: Output format: json, jsonl, plain, markdown, sarif, toml
scan.--output: Write output to a file. Example: -o 'output.txt'
scan.--include-request: Include HTTP request information in output
scan.--include-response: Include HTTP response information in output
scan.--include-all: Include both HTTP request and response information in output (equivalent to --include-request --include-response)
scan.--no-color: Disable colored output (also respects NO_COLOR env var)
scan.--silence: Silence all logs except POC output to STDOUT
scan.--dry-run: Dry-run mode: parse targets, run parameter discovery, and report what would be scanned without sending attack payloads. Outputs target count, discovered parameters, and estimated request count
scan.--stream-findings: Emit each finding (POC + Issue / Payload / Line) the moment it is verified, instead of waiting for end-of-scan. Useful for long scans where you want immediate feedback; off by default so the default flow shows findings after `WRN XSS found N XSS`
scan.--poc-type: POC output type: plain, curl, httpie, http-request
scan.--limit: Limit the number of results to display (must be >=1). Example: --limit 10
scan.--limit-result-type: Filter which finding types count toward --limit: all (default), v (vulnerable), r (reflected), a (AST DOM XSS), i (informational). Example: --limit-result-type v
scan.--only-poc: Filter output to show only specific finding types (comma-separated). Options: v (vulnerable), r (reflected), a (AST DOM XSS), i (informational). Example: --only-poc "v,r"
scan.--baseline: Diff against a previous dalfox JSON/JSONL report and report only findings new since it. The baseline is an ordinary `--format json --output` report. Example: --baseline baseline.json
scan.--baseline-mode: What --baseline does with already-known findings [default: filter]: filter (drop them, so the exit code gates on new findings only) or annotate (keep them and mark each `new`). Example: --baseline-mode annotate
scan.--param: Specify parameter names to analyze (e.g., -p sort -p id:query). Types: query, body, json, cookie, header
scan.--headers: HTTP headers (can be specified multiple times)
scan.--user-agent: Set a custom User-Agent header. Example: --user-agent 'Mozilla/5.0'
scan.--cookie-from-raw: Load cookies from a raw HTTP request file. Example: --cookie-from-raw 'request.txt'
scan.--session-check: Regex that must keep matching the response body for the session to be considered alive (e.g. --session-check 'Sign out'). Authoritative: when set, the built-in heuristics (401/403, login redirect, appearing login form) are not consulted. Without it, session monitoring still runs automatically whenever credentials are supplied via --cookies, --cookie-from-raw, or a Cookie/Authorization header
scan.--session-check-url: Probe this URL instead of the scan target when re-validating the session. Useful when the target itself is public but the app exposes a cheap authenticated endpoint. Example: --session-check-url 'https://app/me'
scan.--on-session-loss: What to do when the session is detected as lost [default: abort]: abort stops the affected target and skips the rest of that host; continue keeps scanning. Either way the target is reported as `incomplete` / SESSION_LOST instead of a misleading "clean"
scan.--include-url: Include only URLs matching these patterns (regex, can be specified multiple times)
scan.--exclude-url: Exclude URLs matching these patterns (regex, can be specified multiple times)
scan.--ignore-param: Ignore specific parameters during scanning (can be specified multiple times)
scan.--out-of-scope: Exclude targets whose domain matches these patterns (supports wildcards, e.g. *.dev.example.com)
scan.--out-of-scope-file: Load out-of-scope domains from a file (one per line, supports wildcards)
scan.--only-discovery: Only perform parameter discovery (skip XSS scanning)
scan.--mining-dict-word: Dictionary analysis with wordlist file path
scan.--remote-wordlists: Fetch remote parameter wordlists from providers (comma-separated). Options: burp, assetnote
scan.--skip-mining-dom: Skip mining parameter names from HTML input id/name attributes. Does NOT disable DOM-XSS static analysis of inline scripts (the `[A]` findings) — use --skip-ast-analysis for that
scan.--timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds (network only; does not bound total scan time)
scan.--scan-timeout: Hard wall-clock cap per target for the payload-injection (scan) stage in seconds. When set, dalfox stops a target's payload-injection stage once this budget is exceeded — useful when many sequential phases each pay the per-request `--timeout` cost against a partially-hung endpoint. Scope note: this caps ONLY the injection stage. The earlier preflight and parameter-analysis (discovery + mining) phases are bounded separately by `--timeout` × request-count, NOT by this wall-clock cap, so a slow target can overshoot this budget during analysis. 0 disables (default)
scan.--rate-limit: Cap the global outbound request rate in requests/second, shared across all workers and targets (0 = unlimited). Unlike --delay (which only spaces a single worker's requests), this bounds the total in-flight burst from workers × concurrent targets — friendlier to shared-IP / edge WAF thresholds. Example: --rate-limit 20
scan.--retries: Retry failed requests on HTTP 5xx and transient transport errors (timeouts, connection resets) up to this many times (0 = off). HTTP 429 is always retried regardless of this value. Example: --retries 2
scan.--retry-delay: Base delay (ms) for the exponential backoff between retries (--retries). Doubles each attempt and is capped internally; a server Retry-After header takes precedence on 429. Example: --retry-delay 500
scan.--insecure: Skip TLS/SSL certificate verification, accepting self-signed, expired, or hostname-mismatched certs. Enabled by default for scanner use; pass `--insecure=false` to enforce certificate validation. Example: --insecure=false
scan.--ignore-return: Ignore specific HTTP status codes during scanning (comma-separated). Example: --ignore-return 302,403,404
scan.--max-concurrent-targets: Maximum number of concurrent targets to scan
scan.--max-targets-per-host: Maximum number of targets per host
scan.--encoders: Specify payload encoders to use (comma-separated). Options: none, url, 2url, 3url, 4url, html, htmlpad, base64, unicode, zwsp. Default: url,html
scan.--remote-payloads: Fetch remote XSS payloads from providers (comma-separated). Options: portswigger, payloadbox
scan.--custom-blind-xss-payload: Load custom blind XSS payloads from a file. Example: --custom-blind-xss-payload 'payloads.txt'
scan.--blind-oob: Enable OOB blind XSS via interactsh. Optional comma-separated server domains (default: public servers). Example: --blind-oob=oast.fun,oast.me
scan.--blind-oob-secret: Auth token (secret) for a self-hosted interactsh server; sent as the Authorization header on register/poll/deregister
scan.--blind-oob-wait: Seconds to keep polling for OOB callbacks after all payloads are sent (default 30; 0 = no extra end-of-scan wait)
scan.--custom-payload: Load custom payloads from a file. Example: --custom-payload 'payloads.txt'
scan.--custom-alert-value: Custom value for alert/prompt/confirm in payloads. Default: "1". Example: --custom-alert-value 'document.domain'
scan.--custom-alert-type: Custom alert function type. Options: none (keep original), str (wrap value in quotes). Default: "none"
scan.--inject-marker: Custom injection point marker. Replace this string with payloads in URL/headers/body. Example: --inject-marker 'FUZZ' with URL 'http://example.com/?q=FUZZ'
scan.--max-payloads-per-param: Cap the number of base payloads tested per parameter (reflection set and DOM-verification set are each capped independently). 0 (default) applies a built-in safety cap of 3000 per set unless --deep-scan is set; pass an explicit value to override, or --deep-scan for a truly unlimited run. Bounds the request fan-out on large attack surfaces and on endpoints that reflect every payload (self-/canonical-link echoes) without verifying. Note: the cap applies to the base catalog; WAF-bypass mutation/encoder expansion and a small set of shared CSP-bypass / tech-specific payloads are added afterwards (and never trimmed), so the actual per-parameter total can exceed this value — substantially so when a WAF bypass strategy is active. Use --deep-scan only to lift the built-in default cap
scan.--deep-scan: Perform deep scanning - test all payloads even after finding XSS
scan.--sxss-url: URL to check for Stored XSS reflection. When omitted with --sxss, auto-detects from form discovery context
scan.--sxss-method: HTTP method for checking Stored XSS (default "GET")
scan.--sxss-retries: Number of times to re-check the Stored XSS URL to handle slow session/content propagation. Each retry waits 500ms * attempt_index
scan.--skip-ast-analysis: Skip AST-based DOM XSS detection — the source→sink analysis of JavaScript in responses that emits [A] findings. This is the flag that silences them; --skip-mining-dom does not
scan.--analyze-external-js: Fetch and AST-analyze same-origin external <script src> bundles for DOM-XSS (off by default to preserve request budget)
scan.--hpp: Enable HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP) — duplicate query params to bypass WAF
scan.--detect-outdated-libs: Also report outdated / known-vulnerable JS libraries (informational, CWE-1104). Off by default: dalfox focuses on verified XSS; this is an opt-in retire.js-style add-on that inspects <script> tags (0 extra requests)
scan.--waf-bypass: WAF bypass mode: auto (detect+bypass), force (use --force-waf), off (detect-only; no payload mutations). Default: auto
scan.--skip-waf-probe: Skip WAF fingerprinting probes (header-only detection, no provocation request)
scan.--force-waf: Force a specific WAF type for bypass strategies (e.g., cloudflare, akamai, modsecurity)
scan.--waf-evasion: Adaptive WAF evasion: when a WAF is detected, randomize inter-request timing (jitter) and escalate a cooldown pause on clusters of blocked responses, instead of the old blunt workers=1/delay=3000 preset. Pairs well with --rate-limit. The per-WAF pacing hint is applied automatically on detection even without this flag
scan.--waf-min-confidence: Discard WAF fingerprints below this confidence (0.0–1.0). Default (0.3) filters weak signals like `Server: Google Frontend` (0.15 — emitted by every Google-hosted property regardless of Cloud Armor) and generic "Request blocked" body markers. Real WAF signatures (Cloudflare 0.9+, AWS WAF 0.95) are kept. Pass `--waf-min-confidence 0.0` to keep every match

server.--config: Path to a config file (TOML or JSON). Overrides default search path
server.--no-color: Disable colored output (also respects NO_COLOR env var)
server.--silence: Silence all logs except POC output to STDOUT
server.--port: Port to run the server on
server.--host: Host to bind the server to
server.--api-key: API key required in X-API-KEY header (or set via DALFOX_API_KEY). Leave empty to disable auth
server.--log-file: Path to a log file to also write logs (plain text, no ANSI colors)
server.--rate-limit: Server-wide cap on each scan's outbound request rate (requests/second; 0 or unset = unlimited). Applied to every submitted scan: a request's own `rate_limit` may be lower but cannot exceed or disable this cap
server.--scan-timeout: Server-wide cap on each scan's total wall-clock runtime, in seconds (0 or unset = unbounded). Applied to every submitted scan: a request's own scan_timeout may be shorter but cannot exceed or disable this cap. Bounds long/deep scans so a single target can't pin a worker indefinitely
server.--max-concurrent-scans: Maximum number of concurrently active (queued + running) scans. Once the cap is hit, new submissions get HTTP 503 until a slot frees. 0 disables the cap (unbounded). Bounds memory + the blocking-pool against a flood of submissions
server.--max-body-bytes: Maximum accepted request-body size (bytes) for POST /scan and /preflight. Replaces axum's implicit 2 MiB default with an explicit, documented bound
server.--allowed-origins: Comma-separated list of allowed origins for CORS. Supports: - "*" wildcard (match all) - exact origins (http://localhost:3000) - "regex:<pattern>" for regex
server.--jsonp: Allow JSONP responses (wrap JSON in callback())

payload.--config: Path to a config file (TOML or JSON). Overrides default search path
payload.--no-color: Disable colored output (also respects NO_COLOR env var)
payload.--silence: Silence all logs except POC output to STDOUT

mcp.--config: Path to a config file (TOML or JSON). Overrides default search path
mcp.--no-color: Disable colored output (also respects NO_COLOR env var)
mcp.--silence: Silence all logs except POC output to STDOUT

not_attempted.raw: dalfox scan scope.txt -f json -o baseline.json      # once, to record the backlog
dalfox scan scope.txt --baseline baseline.json      # every run after
dalfox https://target.app/api -p q -p id:query -p auth:header -p token:cookie
dalfox payload useful-tags     # svg, img, script, ...
dalfox payload special-chars   # < > " ' ` ( ) ... and encoded variants
dalfox payload functions       # confirmable sinks: alert(1), window['alert'](1), ...
dalfox payload awesome-alert   # PoC alerts: alert(document.domain), alert(document.cookie)
dalfox payload dom-clobbering  # DOM clobbering vectors
dalfox payload mxss            # mutation-XSS / sanitizer-bypass payloads
dalfox payload blind           # blind-XSS skeletons ({} = your callback URL)
dalfox payload portswigger     # fetch + print remote list
dalfox payload payloadbox        # fetch PayloadBox XSS list
